title: Local field extension at a specified separable evaluation point
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset S$ be a maximal ideal, put $F=S/\mathfrak p$, and assume $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $K/k$ be a field extension and $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$ a $k$-algebra embedding. Put $C=S\otimes_kK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], define $\epsilon:C\to K$ by $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\iota(\bar s)\lambda$, and put $\mathfrak q=\ker\epsilon$, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$. Then $\epsilon$ is surjective, $\mathfrak q$ is maximal and contracts to $\mathfrak p$ in $S$, and $C$ is a finitely generated $K$-algebra. The rings $A,B$ are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The canonical map $g:A\to B$, $s/u\mapsto(s\otimes1)/(u\otimes1)$, is a faithfully flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Define $\mathfrak r=\ker(F\otimes_kK\to K)$ using $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\iota(a)\lambda$. The $K$-algebra $F\otimes_kK$ is finite-dimensional and reduced, and there are canonical $K$-algebra isomorphisms $B/\mathfrak mB\xrightarrow{\sim}(F\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak r}\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Their composite sends the class of $(s\otimes\lambda)/v$ to $\iota(\bar s)\lambda/\epsilon(v)$ for $v\notin\mathfrak q$. In particular $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak qB$ is the maximal ideal of $B$, and $B/\mathfrak qB\cong K$ via this same evaluation map.

source.place: Tags 0C4Y (lemma-change-fields-flat), proof and clauses (1), (3), (4), and 0C50 (lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified), reduced zero-dimensional fibre argument; here finiteness of F/k gives fibre dimension zero directly, without a dimension-equality assumption.

proof.text: Use the algebra tensor pushout universal property to construct $\epsilon$ from $S\to F\xrightarrow{\iota}K$ and $\mathrm{id}_K$. It sends $1\otimes\lambda$ to $\lambda$, hence is surjective. Thus $C/\mathfrak q\cong K$, so $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. For $s\in S$, $\epsilon(s\otimes1)=0$ exactly when $\bar s=0$, since $\iota$ is injective; therefore $\mathfrak q\cap S=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y, affine setup and evaluation point (explicit specialization).

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ for $S/k$. Expanding each $s$ as a polynomial shows that $s\otimes\lambda$ is a polynomial over $K$ in $s_i\otimes1$; pure tensors generate $C$ additively. Hence these elements generate $C/K$. Every ideal of a field is zero or the unit ideal, so $k,K$ are Noetherian. Apply the finite-type algebra Noetherian theorem to $S/k$ and $C/K$ to conclude that $S,C$ are Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; finite-type base extension by generators.

proof.text: The field-extension base-change theorem makes $S\to C$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, faithfully flat, hence flat. Apply the flat-local-ring-maps theorem to the prime $\mathfrak q$ and its contraction $\mathfrak p$ found in Step 1. It gives Noetherian local rings $A,B$ and the flat local map $g(s/u)=(s\otimes1)/(u\otimes1)$; the denominator is invertible because $u\notin\mathfrak p$. The flat local homomorphism theorem makes $g$ faithfully flat.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y, lemma-change-fields-flat, proof of (1); Algebra Tags 00HT and 00HR.

proof.text: Put $D=F\otimes_kK$ and let $\pi:C\to D$ send $s\otimes\lambda$ to $\bar s\otimes\lambda$. Quotient base change gives $C/\mathfrak pC\cong C\otimes_SF\cong D$: the last isomorphism and its inverse send $(s\otimes\lambda)\otimes a$ to $\bar s a\otimes\lambda$ and $a\otimes\lambda$ to $(1\otimes\lambda)\otimes a$. Thus $\pi$ is onto with kernel $\mathfrak pC$. Construct $e:D\to K$ by $e(a\otimes\lambda)=\iota(a)\lambda$. It is onto, $\mathfrak r=\ker e$ is maximal, and $\epsilon=e\pi$, so $\pi^{-1}\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y, proof of (4); Algebra Tag 00DF and tensor universal property.

proof.text: Write $U=C\setminus\mathfrak q$. Surjectivity of $\pi$ and $\pi^{-1}\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q$ give $\pi(U)=D\setminus\mathfrak r$. Define $\theta:B\to D_{\mathfrak r}$ by $c/u\mapsto\pi(c)/\pi(u)$. This is well defined by the equality-of-fractions relation and is onto by lifting numerator and denominator along $\pi$. Its kernel is $(\mathfrak pC)B$: if $\pi(c)/\pi(u)=0$, there is $w\notin\mathfrak r$ with $w\pi(c)=0$; lift $w$ to $v\notin\mathfrak q$, so $vc\in\mathfrak pC$, and $c/u=(vc)/(vu)\in(\mathfrak pC)B$. The reverse inclusion is immediate. Finally $(\mathfrak pC)B=\mathfrak mB$, since $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ and the denominators from $S\setminus\mathfrak p$ are already units in $B$. Hence $\theta$ induces the first required isomorphism $B/\mathfrak mB\cong D_{\mathfrak r}$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Y, proof of (4), with the quotient-localization argument expanded; Algebra Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient.

proof.text: Choose a finite $k$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $F$. Bilinearity gives $a\otimes\lambda=\sum_i b_i\otimes a_i\lambda$ when $a=\sum_i a_i b_i$, so the $b_i\otimes1$ span $D$ over $K$ and $D$ is finite-dimensional. The finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced theorem, with $L=k$, $K\prime=F$, $E=K$, gives reducedness of $D$. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed finiteness and separability of $F/k$; no separability of $K/k$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0C50, lemma-change-fields-algebraic-unramified, reduced-fibre argument; Algebra Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness.

proof.text: Every prime $P$ of $D$ is maximal: $D/P$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional domain over $K$, and multiplication by any nonzero element is an injective endomorphism, hence surjective, so that element has an inverse. In particular if $P\subseteq\mathfrak r$, both are maximal and equal; thus $\mathfrak r$ is a minimal prime.

source.place: Tag 0C50, zero-dimensional fibre argument; finite dimension replaces the dimension-equality hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply the reduced-minimal-prime localization theorem to $D,\mathfrak r$, using Steps 6 and 7: $D_{\mathfrak r}$ is a field and $\mathfrak rD_{\mathfrak r}=0$. Evaluation extends to $e_{\mathfrak r}:D_{\mathfrak r}\to K$ by $a/w\mapsto e(a)/e(w)$, since $w\notin\mathfrak r$ means $e(w)\ne0$. This unital map from a field is injective and is surjective because it sends $(1\otimes\lambda)/1$ to $\lambda$. It is therefore a $K$-algebra isomorphism. Composing with Step 5 sends $[(s\otimes\lambda)/v]$ to $\iota(\bar s)\lambda/\epsilon(v)$, as asserted. For a general $c/v\in B$ the same formula is $\epsilon(c)/\epsilon(v)$, whose kernel is exactly $\mathfrak qB$. Step 5 and injectivity of $e_{\mathfrak r}$ identify this kernel with $\mathfrak mB$. The localization definition identifies $\mathfrak qB$ as the maximal ideal of $B$, and gives the asserted evaluation identification $B/\mathfrak qB\cong K$.

source.place: Tag 0C50, reduced zero-dimensional local fibre is a field; Algebra Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring.
